definitions.gloss: to triumph; to gloat; to exult in victory
definitions.explanation: To display pride and satisfaction after winning. Often implies showing off one's victory in a way that may be smug or arrogant. Commonly used as a modifier in the form 勝ち誇った (triumphant).

examples.japanese: {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}った{笑|え}みを{浮|う}かべた。
{彼|かれ}は{試合|しあい}に{勝|か}って{勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}っていた。
examples.english: He was gloating after winning the match.

examples.japanese: {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}ったような{態度|たいど}で{相手|あいて}を{見下|みくだ}すのは、スポーツマンシップに{反|はん}する。
examples.english: Looking down on your opponent with a gloating attitude goes against sportsmanship.

notes:
Godan verb (ら row): {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}る・{勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}ります
て-form: {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}って
た-form: {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}った

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}った{顔|かお} (a triumphant face)
- {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}った{笑|え}み (a triumphant smile)
- {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}ったように (as if gloating)
- {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}った{態度|たいど} (a gloating attitude)

USAGE:
Most commonly used in the past-tense modifier form {勝|か}ち{誇|ほこ}った to describe someone's expression, tone, or attitude. Often carries a slightly negative connotation of smugness.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {得意|とくい}になる: To become proud/satisfied — more neutral, doesn't necessarily imply gloating over an opponent.
- {威張|いば}る: To boast, to be arrogant — focuses on the general attitude rather than specifically post-victory behavior.
